<reason>B made the trade-off substantially clearer: greater free-final reach deserves weight, but does not automatically outweigh development and season-long coverage. B honestly answered the symmetrical-evidence challenge and distinguished fragmentation from price exclusion. A established genuine access and cultural benefits, but repeatedly inflated better recruitment into indispensable recruitment and did not meaningfully answer the funding trade-off. B also directly dismantled A’s closing claim that only lost exposure creates irreversible costs.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest rebuttal used A’s own discovery settings: relatives’ televisions and barbecues can also expose newcomers to free regular-season games or household subscription finals. This undermined A’s claim that paywalling marquee games deletes accidental discovery, leaving an incremental benefit that needed comparative justification rather than automatic priority.</best_rebuttal>
